analysis.title: Going With the Global Flows: Softening Resilience, Brewing Rotation
key_insights: Global equity flows are positive but softening from recent highs, as are global ex-US equity flows after a recent pop. Global bond flows remain constructive but are moderating, particularly ex-US. Global money market flows are choppy but picking up, gold is weakening and crypto flows have turned negative (EPFR weekly data as of Oct 28, 2026).

Regional equity flows: Developed Markets are moderating, Emerging Markets are improving, and Western Europe is the weak spot. France, the UK and Germany are in outflow territory, and the modest improvement in Western Europe has begun to reverse.

EM, China and South Korea show positive flows and improving trends. Asia and Japan have shown renewed strength in recent weeks. South Korea monthly flows were firm through August on semiconductor and memory interest, but September saw outflows.

US asset-class flows show hints of rotation. Large Cap and Blend equity flows are positive but below peak. Investment Grade, TIPS and Muni bond flows are positive and improving, and US Treasury funds have seen steady inflows through summer and fall, with a modest outflow in the latest week.

Within US equities, Mid Cap flows are negative, Growth and Value give no strong signals, and Small Cap is weak but stabilizing. RBC reads the Small Cap improvement as a market searching for rotation destinations rather than a risk-on signal.

US investor base: ETF, passive, institutional, domestic-domiciled and foreign-domiciled equity flows are positive. Retail, non-ETF and active flows are weak, with retail still net sellers. Active redemptions are slowing a bit.

DM sector flows show only isolated pockets of strength. Energy and Health Care/Biotech have strong flow levels with stable-to-improving trends. Consumer, REITs and Utilities have reversed sharply and are negative again.

Financials and Industrials have been weak but showed signs of stabilization in the latest weekly data. Tech and Telecom flows are positive but volatile. The tech four-week average is inflated by a sharp inflow several weeks ago.
Regional sector divergences: US Financials are weaker than DM broadly. European Utilities are stronger than DM broadly, while European Financials, Industrials and Health Care are notably weaker.

Factor flows: all factor funds except low volatility show positive weekly and four-week average inflows (momentum, quality, defensive, dividend yield). Low volatility has negative four-week flows but a small weekly inflow. Momentum flows are very choppy.

Thematic flows show previous hot trades cooling. Aerospace & Defense, BDCs, Industrial Metals, Rare Earths and Space & Satellite have faded from dramatic surges, some turning negative. AI flows are positive but well off prior highs, and semiconductors are volatile but positive.

Cybersecurity is a standout with positive and accelerating flows. Software flows have lagged, with the four-week average drifting lower, which RBC says means AI enthusiasm has not translated into broad software inflows.

Leveraged and inverse thematic flows: leveraged AI flows are subdued with a slightly negative four-week average. Leveraged semis flows have recovered after summer outflows, and inverse semis inflows have returned. Inverse software flows are back in positive territory, indicating bearish positioning remains.

Canada: equity flows have been strong this year and have eased a bit from highs. Large Cap and Blend inflows persist, Small Cap outflows persist but are improving, Value and Growth have deteriorated, and passive flows are much stronger than active.

Sustainability: weekly sustainable equity fund flows have turned negative again, and sustainable bond flows are easing, turning slightly negative for Europe-domiciled funds last week. Most themes are in outflow except Nuclear & Uranium (slightly positive, off highs), Cybersecurity and Gender funds.

AI and electrification-linked sustainable themes (Smart Grid/Power, Sustainable Infrastructure, Sustainable Tech, Clean Energy) have weakened from their earlier-2026 highs. EV flows turned sharply negative again.

Commodities: energy remains tied to the Iran conflict, and Brent flows reflect growing attention to crude's post-midterm dynamics. Natural gas has the strongest inflows, Brent improved with the August/September price recovery, and WTI remains mixed.

Metals flows have mostly faded. Gold momentum is fading as September monthly strength was offset by recent weekly outflows. Silver is relatively weak after a strong 2025 to early 2026. Copper and nickel lag, and aluminum is stable but weaker.

Agriculture lags generally. Livestock is the sole leader with positive momentum, while corn, wheat, soybean and sugar are declining after mid-year peaks. Overall early-year commodity momentum is fading outside energy and possibly livestock, which RBC says signals investor caution.

Crypto is the only global asset class lagging: monthly flows ticked up in September but remain well below the 2020-21 surge, and weekly flows have worsened with the four-week average pointing to weaker near-term momentum.
Gold flows in the current cycle came close to matching the highs of the COVID era on both monthly and weekly measures, but weekly flows have now turned negative.

crypto_views: Global crypto funds are the only major asset class lagging in EPFR flow data, with weekly flows worsening and the four-week average pointing to weaker near-term momentum.
Monthly crypto fund flows ticked up in September but remain well below the 2020-21 surge.
risk_factors: Western Europe equity flows are reversing a modest improvement and are in outflow territory across France, the UK and Germany.
Fading flows in previously hot themes (Aerospace & Defense, Rare Earths, Space & Satellite, Industrial Metals, BDCs) show speculative momentum cooling.
Gold weekly outflows and weak crypto flows indicate fading demand for alternative assets.
Commodity markets remain subject to headline risk and uncertainty tied to the Iran conflict.
vol_and_positioning: Leveraged AI fund flows are subdued, with a slightly negative four-week average, suggesting investor caution rather than aggressive leveraged exposure.
Inverse software fund flows have moved back into positive territory, suggesting bearish positioning persists as software sentiment remains weak.
Leveraged semiconductor flows recovered after large summer outflows and improved again in the latest updates. Inverse semis inflows returned after a period of outflows.
Global derivative fund flows are positive but with a slightly weaker trend. Long/short fund flows are positive but have eased, with a weaker weekly trend.
US retail equity flows remain negative while institutional and passive flows are positive, though institutional demand has been weaker lately.
geopolitical: Energy flows remain linked to the Iran conflict and its trajectory, with Brent flows reflecting attention to its likely path.
Crude oil dynamics after the US midterm elections are cited as a growing consideration for Brent flows.

tension_points.bull_case: Small Cap flows are showing signs of stabilization, which could point to risk-on buying.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC views the nascent Small Cap improvement as less of a risk-on signal and more of a market searching for rotation destinations. Small Cap monthly flows remain weak and recent weekly outflows have returned.

theme_stances.key_argument: Global equity flows are positive but clearly softening from recent highs, as are global ex-US equity flows.
theme_stances.evidence: global equity story appears to be one of moderating resilience
